mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters indicates strengthening economic demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of periods with positive GDP growth, or the correlation between GDP growth and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in industrial production by more than 1% in a month indicates supply chain disruptions or reduced manufacturing output, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are negatively impacted.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between INDPRO declines and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts and real personal consumption expenditures signals a strengthening demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer confidence and economic activity improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of periods with positive signals from both HOUST and RSAFS, or the joint correlation between these indicators and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and corporate earnings are expected to improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of periods with positive signals from both PAYEMS and UNRATE, or the joint correlation between these indicators and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the consumer price index by more than 0.5% in a month signals a potential deflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings and economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between CPIAUCSL decreases and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP growth and a simultaneous decrease in the unemployment rate signal a robust economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer confidence and corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of periods with positive signals from both GDPC1 and UNRATE, or the joint correlation between these indicators and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
